observations.code_quote: **Customer analytics owns the billing chart render.** Each billing chart is multi-series on one shared axis, so a small-magnitude series (e.g. feature flag requests) is a flat sliver against large ones (events/enhanced persons) and can't be read. To offer per-series show/hide **without touching shared data-viz code**, `AccountBillingChart` renders the saved insight's SQL chart directly via `@posthog/quill-charts` instead of an embedded `<Query>`/DataVisualization. It reuses `dataVisualizationLogic` read-only for fetch + SQL-results→series parsing, and renders via `sqlLineGraphAdapter.ts`'s pure builders — the same series building, render dispatch, and line/bar/combo config building (per-column formatting, area fills, right-axis routing, goal and trend lines, percent stacks, plus the 200-series render cap applied locally) the SQL insight chart uses — while staying off that chart's React layer (`SqlChart`/`useSqlChartModel`). Chart-semantics changes belong in the adapter (covered by `sqlLineGraphAdapter.test.ts`), not here. Hidden series are injected into quill's controlled `legend.hiddenKeys` (excluded from drawing and scales; the rest rescale into the freed space). `AccountBillingSeriesToggle` is the control: a compact chip row under each chart, one chip per series colored to match its line/bar (items come from `legendItemsFromSeries` over the same `buildSeries` output the chart draws, so keys and colors can't drift), plus Select all / Clear all buttons at the end of the row that show or hide every series at once (`setAllSeriesHidden`, dispatched with the chart's own key list). The hidden-keys state lives in `accountBillingLogic` (`ephemeralHiddenSeriesKeysByShortId`, keyed per insight because the spend tab renders two) — per-view only: never written to the saved insight, reset on date change, gone on row collapse. Queries whose shape `AccountBillingChart` can't render (non-DataViz, table/number/pie displays, series breakdowns — see `canRenderBillingChart`) fall back to the embedded `<Query>` with no chips. Billing queries stay embedded in both the account list and detail scene: the account and date filter supply SQL variables, so their read-only pickers remain hidden. Embedded SQL charts use their container height instead of the standalone insight viewport height.
